title: Remarks in accepting a card of membership in the Press Club at Milwaukee, Wisconsin
paragraphs: I accept with all gratitude the honorary membership in your club. I am so glad that I was here some years ago and that I am able to come back now, and as we are speaking among ourselves with no reporters present, I want to say just one word with all my heart. I have found that if I felt I wished to tell something to someone whom [?] I knew would not repeat it, if there was something that it was essential to keep which I wished [?] to tell to some one with whom I knew it would be kept sacred I could take any honorable man connected with the press with absolute certainty that my faith would be justified. (Applause.)

Among the closest friends that I have made in every station which I have held; where I wanted to test the men's [?] friendship to see if they had the stuff in them that made it worth while being friends with them; in every such station, whether in the army or as governor or now as President, I have found that it was among the men of your profession that I got some of the closest and staunchest of my friends. I won't say that I have always gotten along well with all the gentlemen of your profession, but I wish to say with all the emphasis possible that taken on the whole there has been no more honorable body, no more upright body than the men of your profession, of the stamp whom you yourselves would have in this club, and I greet you and thank you for having me here this evening. (Cheers and applause.)
